accuracy.evidence: Checked against NC 2013 Y4 sound ('identify how sounds are made, associating some of them with something vibrating'; 'recognise that vibrations from sounds travel through a medium to the ear') and NGSS 1-PS4-1 ('vibrating materials can make sound and sound can make materials vibrate'), which is the exact two-way claim of the topic. Vibrating parts checked: drum membrane (skin), guitar strings (the soundhole only radiates), larynx / vocal folds (voice box), tuning fork prongs (the classic water-splash demonstration). The rice-on-a-drum demo is the topic's own evidence line. Weaker sound far away is stated as 'weak by then' without a wrong inverse-square claim. Parameterised items checked at range corners: p2 n*s 20..250, p4 r-j 1..18, m6 a-b 1..8, m9 n*s 40..240.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented primary sound misconceptions (Nuffield/ASE primary science misconception lists; Hapkiewicz on sound): the striker makes the sound (drumstick card, WHYNOT drumstick, m2); the hole or body of a guitar makes it (round hole card, tag hole, m3); a sound continues after the source stops (step 2 prediction 'keeps going', m7); vibrations must be visible (fork step prediction 'nothing: it is not moving', tags still/none, m5); breath not sound moves the rice (tag blow, m4, adult card test); ears make sound (singer card, tag ears).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagvib is about the vibration itself: a plucked band that blurs and decays, a finger that damps it, choosing the vibrating part of three sources, sound travelling to a drum skin that throws rice (distance matters), and a hidden fork vibration revealed by water. flagloud varies how hard you hit; flagpitch varies how fast; neither has damping, sound-to-object transfer or the hidden-vibration reveal. Max 6-shingle similarity 3.6% (with flag_coin.js), under 3% against every older lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each idea is discovered before it is named: the band only twangs while it moves and the label flips to 'Still: no sound' as the motion decays; touching stops it at once; far shouts make the rice wobble only and the narration says to move closer, near shouts make it jump; dipping an unstruck fork gives 'the water stays still' while a struck one splashes. The completion text then states the rule (no vibration, no sound; sound makes things vibrate).

predictions.evidence: Four predictions with tempting wrong options that the lab disproves: where the twang comes from ('the box' / 'your finger'; only the band moves on screen), holding the band ('keeps going'; sound stops at once), shouting at the drum ('stays still: nothing touched it'; the rice jumps), and the fork in water ('nothing: it is not moving'; it splashes).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Twelve distinct slip messages in slip(): loud (louder is not vibration), oneway (must go back and forth), hole, finger, warm, tired, hear (rice cannot hear), blow (breath too far away), nothing and ears (the buzz is in the throat), still and none (too fast to see). The find step adds a per-part message for each wrong part (WHYNOT), and the drum and fork steps give their own feedback for far shouts and unstruck forks.

readability.evidence: validate_lessons passes for the family audience (kid FK well under 5, adult under 10). Kid text uses short sentences and everyday words (shake, buzz, back and forth); 'vibration' is defined on first use. Canvas labels are 13-18 px bold dark text on pale cards and shrink to fit at 360 px; buttons are 1-3 words (Pluck the band, Shout!, Dip in water).

no_filler.evidence: Content gate passes (no banned phrases; explanation overlap 0.6% at most, with Pitch of Sounds). Kid paragraphs: what a vibration is; stopping it; three sources; sound makes things vibrate. Adult paragraphs: curriculum statements and key words; named mistakes with a fair test for the breath slip; boundary with the loud/quiet and pitch lessons; what the lab does.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots before and after Show me at 360 px Android (light) and iPhone 13 (dark) plus desktop. First pass clipped the third part card on the find step and drew the singer overlapping the drum; fixed by moving the cards up, shrinking the drum icon on narrow screens, capping the singer at half width and drawing sound rings only while shouting. Part cards are full-width, 46+ px tall tap targets; control buttons wrap below the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button ('Pull the band and let go', 'Put a finger on the band', 'The drum skin', 'Move the singer closer to the drum', 'Shout at the drum', 'Tap the fork on the rubber block', 'Dip the fork in the water'). tell() updates the canvas aria-label and the narration after each action. walk.cjs: desktop and iPhone 13 complete all 5 tasks with Show me, the challenge shows, axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in both themes, no console errors.
